priorities.name: Quiet space for calls and focused work
priorities.issue: There are too few spaces to take calls, so most people are on the open floor during meetings, making it noisy for everyone.
whatItLooksLike: There are limited spaces where calls can be taken so most people are on the floor while holding or attending meetings and it can be quite noisy.

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (87/100); focused-work friction 27/100 (56% under-supported).
Noise & Distraction: 65 people (22% of respondents), 90 comments, 68% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Assess call/quiet-space capacity and etiquette against demand before adding enclosed space.
priorities.siteMustDo: Track call-space demand vs. availability and pilot a quiet/call-etiquette norm; size any gap for Workplace Solutions.

priorities.name: On-site food and beverage options
priorities.issue: Food options are seen as poor — the frozen/market selection isn't useful — and F&B is cited well above the company norm here.
whatItLooksLike: There should better options made available for buying food. The frozen section is not useful.

evidence.text: Food & Beverage: 77 people (26% of respondents), 101 comments, 46% negative; raised by 26% of respondents vs 19% company-wide.
On-site food/beverage availability friction is 25/100 (46% under-supported); Service Level is below the company average (68.4 ± 2 vs 75.6).

priorities.proposedAction: Review the F&B vendor's offering, hours and stocking with the Food & Beverage team against what associates actually want.
priorities.siteMustDo: Gather the specific gaps (options, hours, freshness) and bring them to the Food & Beverage team for a vendor review.

priorities.name: Workstation equipment and desk adjustability
priorities.issue: Keyboards and station equipment aren't routinely checked (stuck/dead keys), and desks don't lower enough for smaller associates.
whatItLooksLike: Maybe having routine checks on the equipment in the rooms and stations would be nice. Sometimes for examples the keyboards may not be working or have stuck keys which can make working a bit more difficult.
desks need to be able to lower more for smaller people

evidence.text: Hardware: 59 people (20% of respondents), 88 comments, 61% negative; Desk Availability: 52 people (18% of respondents), 67 comments, 57% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Institute routine equipment checks and confirm desk-height adjustability options for smaller associates.
priorities.siteMustDo: Run a station-by-station equipment check and confirm/adjust desk-height range where needed.

priorities.name: Private space for confidential conversations
priorities.issue: Managers and associates handling sensitive matters have to get up and find a room for each confidential conversation, and booking a conference room doesn't work for short, unplanned ones.
whatItLooksLike: I have to pick up and move to have a private conversation (termination, salary, performance mgmt discussion). That can be frustrating to be up an down through out the day.
…Reserving a conference room is not a viable option when you have sporadic meetings that involve confidential information.
Lack of secure/discretionary space to discuss issues related to CEO complaints.

evidence.text: Availability of spaces that support discretion: Under Supported — friction 28/100 (50% under-supported).
Tasks requiring discretion: Under Supported — friction 23/100 (42% under-supported).
Privacy & Confidentiality: 59 people (20% of respondents), 80 comments, 60% negative.
Distinct from P1 (noise for calls and focused work): this is confidentiality for conversations, which room-hold rules can address first.

priorities.proposedAction: Check utilization of the enclosed rooms and hold a few small ones for short, walk-up confidential conversations (no all-day bookings) before considering any new enclosed space.
priorities.siteMustDo: Measure how often a private room is unavailable when needed over two weeks, pilot the walk-up rooms, and escalate a sized gap if the pilot doesn't close it.

priorities.name: Escalator and entry-door reliability
priorities.issue: The escalator from the 1st to the 2nd floor and the side entry door break down repeatedly and stay out of service for long periods.
whatItLooksLike: Escalator from 1st floor to 2nd floor is ALWAYS broken
We have significantly recurring issues with the side entry door and the escalators, which is incredibly frustrating.
It can be an inconvenience when some of the doors do not work or the escalator is broken. Especially the escalator as it takes forever for it to be operational again.

evidence.text: Building Operations: 34 people (12% of respondents), 41 comments, 63% negative — raised by 12% of respondents vs 4% company-wide.
Reliability of building operations: Under Supported — friction 18/100 (42% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Pull the escalator and entry-door work-order history, escalate the repeat failures for a repair-vs-replace assessment, and post alternate-route signage while units are down.
priorities.siteMustDo: Compile the outage history, request the repair-vs-replace assessment, and report downtime monthly until it is resolved.

protectWhatIsWorking.evidence: 44% positive and 24% negative across 25 comments from 20 people — community managers are praised by name
protectWhatIsWorking.note: Maintain the current service level and monitor performance.

assumptions: Richmond is below the company average overall (Index 67 ± 2 vs 69.0) and on Service Level (68.4 vs 75.6); food and beverage is raised by 26% of respondents here, more than at the other sites beyond chance.
The Richmond↔Norfolk comparison (outdoor walking areas, escalators) is associate-reported and worth an onsite check.
